prs.title: Docs: Document Stencil import injection for static builds
prs.manualTesting:
**1. The rendered docs**

1. Build/serve the docs site from this branch.
2. Go to *Get started → Frameworks → Web Components + Vite → FAQ*. "How do I use Stencil with static Storybook builds?" should appear above "How do I manually install the Web Components framework?", with the snippet labeled `stencil.config.ts`.
3. Go to *Sharing → Publish Storybook* with the renderer selector set to **Web Components**. A **Troubleshooting** section should appear between "Build Storybook for older browsers" and "Publish Storybook with Chromatic".
4. Switch the renderer selector to React — that section should disappear, since it is wrapped in `<If renderer="web-components">`.

**2. That the documented workaround actually works**

Steps, using the reproduction repo from #25704:

1. Clone https://github.com/vivere-dally/sb-stencil and `npm ci`.
2. `npm run build && npm run build-storybook`, then serve `storybook-static` (with caching disabled — a caching static server will mask rebuilds).
3. Open `iframe.html?id=components-my-component--example`. The story is blank.
4. Add the `extras` flag from these docs to `stencil.config.ts`.
5. Rebuild both, serve again. The story renders.

I ran this before opening the update. Results:

| Stencil | `extras` flag | `*.entry.js` chunk in `storybook-static/assets` | Story render |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.11.0 | *(none)* | absent | blank — `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: /assets/my-component.entry.js` |
| 4.11.0 | `experimentalImportInjection` | `my-component.entry-MNJrIq1y.js` | `Hello, World! I'm AAA BBB CCC` |
| 4.43.5 | *(none)* | absent | — |
| 4.43.5 | `enableImportInjection` | `my-component.entry-CrMxYaM5.js` | `Hello, World! I'm AAA BBB CCC` |

Both documented flags fix the built output on their respective Stencil versions, and the failure still reproduces on current Stencil (4.43.5) without them. The two no-flag rows were confirmed by the missing entry chunk; the 4.11.0 no-flag row was additionally confirmed in-browser with the console error above.

prs.title: Core: Fix DEP0205 deprecation warning for module.register() on Node.js 26
prs.manualTesting:
This bug is Node-version-gated in two directions — it only reproduces on Node 26, and the fix's fallback only matters below Node 22.15 — so a full manual test needs to span multiple Node versions, not just one:

1. Build this branch's `core` package: `yarn nx run core:compile`.
2. Scaffold or open any project with a TypeScript `.storybook/main.ts` (e.g. `npx storybook@latest init` in a fresh Vite + React + TypeScript app), and point its `storybook`/`@storybook/*` dependencies at this branch's build (e.g. `yarn link`, or by copying `code/core/dist` + `code/core/package.json` over `node_modules/storybook/`).
3. **On Node.js 26** (e.g. `nvm install 26` or `brew install node@26`): run `NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-deprecation npm run storybook` (or `storybook build`). Confirm no `[DEP0205]` warning is printed — this is the original bug from #35336.
4. **On Node.js 20.19.x or 22.12–22.14.x** (below the `registerHooks` cutoff): run the same command. Confirm it does **not** crash with `SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:module' does not provide an export named 'registerHooks'` — this would be a regression from a naive fix.
5. On both Node versions, confirm the build/dev server otherwise works normally and correctly loads `.storybook/main.ts` (real stories show up, not an empty/failed build).

I verified this exact matrix (20.19.2 and 22.12.0 for the `register()` fallback path; 24.18.0, 25.9.0, and 26.0.0 for the `registerHooks()` path) by swapping the built `core` package's `dist` into a real Storybook project and running `storybook build`/`dev` on each. A minimal reproduction repo for the original bug (unpatched) is at https://github.com/alexismo/storybook-dep0205-node26-repro.

prs.title: Evals: Tweak CI setup for cost efficiency and peace of mind
prs.manualTesting:
1. On a test PR from a branch in this repository, add `agent-eval:eval`. The gate thread appears on a changed file, with the marker comment, the head SHA and the scope line.
2. Let the run pass without pushing. The thread body shows the pass summary and the thread is resolved.
3. Push a new commit. The thread is reopened ("evals required for new head") and evals do not start.
4. Add an unrelated label such as `qa:needed` while an eval is running. No new eval starts and the running eval is not cancelled.
5. Remove and re-add `agent-eval:eval` (or run `workflow_dispatch` with `pr_number`). Evals run again and update the same thread; no second gate thread appears.
6. Add `agent-eval:all-evals` or `agent-eval:storybook-latest`. The matching `EVAL_*` flag is set and the label appears in the thread's scope line. An undeclared label such as `agent-eval:foo` or `agent-eval:review` gives a warning annotation and has no effect.
7. Make a run fail or cancel it. The thread stays open with the failure summary and run links.
8. Run `workflow_dispatch` on `next`. No PR thread is touched, the playground deploys to production, and a summary is posted to `#sb-monitoring`.

prs.manualTesting:
No token needed: the script runs against a local copy of the skills repo.

1. Set up, from a checkout of this branch with dependencies installed:

   ```bash
   rm -rf /tmp/skills-remote.git /tmp/skills-check
   git clone --mirror https://github.com/storybookjs/skills /tmp/skills-remote.git
   export SKILLS_REPO_URL=file:///tmp/skills-remote.git
   ```

2. Sync `v11.0.0-alpha.1` the way CI does, from the release tag. The skills repo already has this version, so expect `already matches` and `4db2487`:

   ```bash
   git fetch origin tag v11.0.0-alpha.1
   VERSION=11.0.0-alpha.1 STORYBOOK_REF=v11.0.0-alpha.1 node ./scripts/release/sync-skills.ts
   ```

3. `VERSION=11.0.0-alpha.2 node ./scripts/release/sync-skills.ts`. Expect `next is at <sha>, tagged v11.0.0-alpha.2`. That is a new commit, because the `stories` skill changed since `v11.0.0-alpha.1`. Once the first real sync after merge has run, expect `already matches` here instead.
4. `VERSION=11.0.0-alpha.3 node ./scripts/release/sync-skills.ts`. Expect `already matches`, with the same sha.
5. Run step 4 again. Expect the same output and no error.

prs.title: Addon Vitest: Restart the test runner after its child process dies
prs.manualTesting:
1. Run a sandbox: `yarn task --task sandbox --start-from auto --template react-vite/default-ts`, and start Storybook.
2. Run the tests for one component from its context menu.
3. Find the Vitest child: `pgrep -f "addon-vitest/dist/node/vitest"`, then `kill -9 <pid>`.
4. The testing widget shows "Component tests didn't complete" with a "View full error" link.
5. Run the component's tests again. They run, and `pgrep` shows a new child.
6. Start a full run, and `kill -9` the child while it runs. The widget shows the error state and does not keep spinning. The next run works.

Done on the Chromatic webapp (3,840 stories), branch build at `e04f47c`:

| Step | This branch | `next` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kill -9` the child between runs | "Component tests didn't complete" | Still shows the old "Ran 7 tests" |
| Next focused run | Runs 7 tests in a new child | Nothing runs; no child process |
| Two quick clicks on Run tests, no child running | One child starts | One child starts (the double start came from #36421's pre-spawn reads) |
| `kill -9` during a full run | Error state; no spinner left | Could not get here: after the first kill no run starts |
| Next focused run | Runs 7 tests in a new child | – |

After the kill, on this branch:

prs.title: Docs: Record the argTypes removal and four missing breaking changes in the migration guide
prs.manualTesting:
| Command | What it checks | Run from |
| ------- | -------------- | -------- |
| `yarn docs:check` | Every rule in `scripts/docs/check-docs.ts` for `docs/`, including cross-file `#fragment` targets | repo root |
| `audit.py` below | Which Storybook 11 `MIGRATION.md` sections the guide never mentions | repo root |
| The `comm` pipeline below | Every `MIGRATION.md` anchor the guide links to, against GitHub's own rendered heading ids | repo root |

1. Check out this branch and run `yarn docs:check` from the repository root. It prints `✅ Docs check: no errors found.`

2. Confirm the five added entries are the ones that were missing, and that nothing else was dropped. Save this as `audit.py` at the repository root and run `python3 audit.py`:

   ```python
   import re
   mig = open('MIGRATION.md').read().split('\n')
   start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(mig) if l.startswith('## From version 10.x to 11.0.0'))
   end = next(i for i, l in enumerate(mig) if i > start and l.startswith('## From version 10.5'))
   guide = open('docs/releases/migration-guide.mdx').read()
   slug = lambda h: re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9 -]', '', h.lower()).replace(' ', '-')
   for l in mig[start:end]:
       if l.startswith('### ') and slug(l[4:]) not in guide:
           print('not in the guide:', l[4:])
   ```

   On this branch it prints the six deliberate entries from the table above. On `next` it prints eleven.

3. Confirm every `MIGRATION.md` link the guide adds lands on a real heading. This asks GitHub to render `MIGRATION.md` and compares its heading ids against the links in the diff, so it does not depend on reimplementing the slugger:

   ```sh
   gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.html" \
     "/repos/storybookjs/storybook/contents/MIGRATION.md?ref=next" \
     | grep -o 'id="user-content-[^"]*"' | sed 's/id="user-content-//; s/"//' | sort -u > /tmp/anchors.txt
   git diff origin/next -U0 docs/releases/migration-guide.mdx | grep '^+' \
     | grep -o 'MIGRATION.md#[^)]*' | sed 's|MIGRATION.md#||' | sort -u \
     | while read a; do grep -qx "$a" /tmp/anchors.txt && echo "OK   $a" || echo "MISS $a"; done
   ```

   It prints `OK` five times.

4. Confirm the one same-page anchor resolves on the rendered page. Open the migration guide, and in **Major breaking changes** click **`argTypes` removed from loaders, `beforeEach`, `play` and `afterEach`**. It jumps to the new section further down the page.

prs.title: Svelte: Turn on the built-in Svelte CSF and stop using the addon
prs.manualTesting:
1. Generate the `svelte-vite/default-ts` sandbox: `yarn task sandbox --template svelte-vite/default-ts --start-from auto`.
2. Check that its `package.json` doesn't list `@storybook/addon-svelte-csf`, and that the template stories show and render.
3. Add `'@storybook/addon-svelte-csf'` to `addons` in `.storybook/main.ts`, and check that Storybook stops with `SB_SVELTE_CSF_PRESET_0001`.

**The check works with the real addon.** In the same app, I installed `@storybook/addon-svelte-csf@5.1.5` and added it with `legacyTemplate: true`. `storybook dev` and Vitest both stopped with the addon error, naming `@storybook/svelte-vite` and the removed legacy syntax.

**Strict pnpm works.** I tested a new `svelte-ts` Vite app with pnpm 12, `hoist: false` and an empty `publicHoistPattern`, so the app can only import its direct dependencies. I ran `storybook init` against a local registry with this branch's packages.
- Without the `resolveId` hook in commit 2, `storybook build` failed: `Rolldown failed to resolve import "@storybook/svelte/internal/svelte-csf/create-runtime-stories" from "./src/stories/Header.stories.svelte"`. The compiler adds that import to every stories file, and the app doesn't depend on `@storybook/svelte`.
- With it, `storybook build` passes. In `storybook dev`, the button, header and page stories render, and the autodocs page shows the source code, with no browser errors.
- **No re-optimization or reload, from an empty cache.** I deleted `node_modules/.cache` and `node_modules/.vite`, and ran with `DEBUG=vite:deps`. In `storybook dev`, Vite optimized once at startup ("the scanner found every used dependency") and logged nothing more while I opened all 11 entries. A marker on the preview's `window` survived every story switch, so the preview never reloaded. In Vitest, all 8 story tests pass with the same single optimization.

**Hoisted installs don't reload either.** CI showed that the `svelte-vite` and `svelte-kit` sandbox Vitest jobs reloaded mid-run, because Vite found the runtime late. With `order: 'pre'` on that hook, from an empty cache, Vitest passes in both sandboxes (209 and 228 tests) with no late optimization. In `storybook dev`, three Svelte CSF stories render with one page load each and no late optimization in the `DEBUG=vite:deps` log.

prs.title: CLI: Detect internal manager-api specifier in set-config-layout automigration
prs.manualTesting:
1. Create a scratch project with `.storybook/main.js` containing `export default { stories: [] }` and `.storybook/manager.js` containing:
   ```js
   import { addons } from 'storybook/internal/manager-api';

   addons.setConfig({ theme, showNav: false, showPanel: true, panelPosition: 'right' });
   ```
2. Run `npx storybook@latest automigrate set-config-layout` (published 11.0.0-alpha.6 shows the bug: exit 0, "No migrations were applicable", file untouched).
3. Check out this branch, build the CLI (`cd code && yarn build sb-cli --prod --no-watch`), run `node code/lib/cli-storybook/dist/bin/index.js automigrate set-config-layout` in the scratch project.
4. Expect: "🔎 found a 'set-config-layout' migration", exit 0, and `manager.js` rewritten to
   ```js
   import { addons } from 'storybook/internal/manager-api';

   addons.setConfig({
     theme,

     layout: {
       showNav: false,
       showPanel: true,
       panelPosition: 'right'
     }
   });
   ```
   — byte-identical (apart from the specifier) to the output for a `storybook/manager-api` import.
5. Repeat step 3 with a file that imports from `storybook/manager-api` to confirm public-specifier behavior is unchanged.
6. Optional (reporting path): with the internal-specifier import and `addons.setConfig({ showNav: false, layout: { showNav: true } })` (a conflict), expect exit 1 and a `automigrations-summary.md` entry naming the file and reason — not a silent skip.

Verification captured while developing (fixture projects run against published `11.0.0-alpha.6` before, and the local built CLI after):

| Case | Before (alpha.6) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storybook/internal/manager-api` | exit 0, "No migrations were applicable", file untouched | detected, rewritten, exit 0 |
| `storybook/manager-api` (control) | detected, rewritten, exit 0 | unchanged behavior |
| internal specifier + top-level/nested conflict | silent skip (not detected) | detected, file reported as skipped with per-file reason in `automigrations-summary.md`, exit 1 |

prs.title: Build: Stop auto-closing issues whose reproduction link is a local Storybook
prs.manualTesting:
The `issues` trigger always runs the workflow from the default branch, so the end-to-end check can only happen after merge. Before merge, the detection logic can be exercised locally:

1. Run `zizmor` on the workflow and confirm the only finding is the pre-existing `issue_comment` trigger warning:

   ```bash
   uvx zizmor .github/workflows/triage.yml
   ```

2. Paste the `script:` block from the new step into a Node ≥ 20 REPL with stubs for `context` and `core`, e.g.:

   ```js
   process.env.REPRO_LINK_SECTION = '### Reproduction link(.*)### Reproduction steps';
   const core = { info: console.log, setOutput: (k, v) => console.log('output', k, v) };
   const context = { payload: { issue: { body: '### Reproduction link\n\nhttp://127.0.0.1:6006/?path=/story/x\n\n### Reproduction steps\n\n1.' } } };
   // ...then the script block
   ```

   Expected: `output local true` for `http://127.0.0.1:6006/...`, `http://localhost:6006/...`, `localhost:6006`; `output local false` for `https://github.com/foo/bar`, `http://localhost.evil.com`, `http://app.localhost:3000` and a missing link.

After merge to `next`:

3. Open a bug report with `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/example-button--primary` as the reproduction link. Expected: the issue stays open, the "Detect local reproduction link" step logs `skipping nissuer`, and the nissuer step is shown as skipped.
4. Open a bug report with `https://github.com/storybookjs/this-repo-does-not-exist` as the reproduction link. Expected: still auto-closed with the `needs reproduction` label and the invalid-link comment, as today.
5. Add the `good first issue` label to any issue. Expected: the bot still posts the good-first-issue comment.

Areas worth extra scrutiny: the `if:` condition on the nissuer step must leave it running for `labeled` and `issue_comment` events, where the detection step is skipped and its output is empty.

prs.title: SvelteKit: Automigrate sveltekit_experimental to beforeEach
prs.manualTesting:
1. Make a sandbox: `yarn task sandbox --template svelte-kit/skeleton-ts --start-from auto`, then `cd ../storybook-sandboxes/svelte-kit-skeleton-ts`.
2. Add stories with the old API. Copy the old template stories and their components into the sandbox:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p src/stories/old-api
   for f in State Navigation Hrefs Forms; do git -C <repo> show 8bddc82ac02:code/frameworks/sveltekit/template/stories_svelte-kit-skeleton-ts/modules/$f.svelte > src/stories/old-api/$f.svelte; done
   for f in forms hrefs navigation state; do git -C <repo> show 8bddc82ac02:code/frameworks/sveltekit/template/stories_svelte-kit-skeleton-ts/modules/$f.stories.js | sed "s#stories/frameworks/sveltekit/modules/#old-api/#" > src/stories/old-api/$f.stories.js; done
   ```
   Also add a `.stories.svelte` file that sets `sveltekit_experimental` in `defineMeta()` and on a `<Story>`, for example the "before" example of the MIGRATION.md section.
3. Run `yarn storybook build` and open an old story, for example `old-api/state` "Page". It fails with `SvelteKitMockParametersRemovedError`.
4. Run `npx storybook automigrate sveltekit-mocking-before-each`. Check that:
   - each migrated file changed only where the parameters were, where `beforeEach` is, and in its imports;
   - the code matches the MIGRATION.md table;
   - a file that can't be migrated is listed in `automigrations-summary.md`, with the line and the reason.
5. Build again and open the stories. They render, and the `play` functions of `old-api/navigation`, `old-api/hrefs` and `old-api/state` pass in the Interactions panel. Expected exception: the `old-api/forms` "Enhance" `play` checks its spy right after the click. The submit flow now runs async, so that check fails until it awaits.
6. Run the automigration again. It changes nothing.
7. Areas most likely to regress: Svelte files with unusual formatting, stories that also set `beforeEach`, and TypeScript stories with typed callbacks. Run `yarn check` (svelte-check) before and after the automigration and compare.

prs.title: Test: Fix the context userEvent in insecure contexts
prs.manualTesting:
You need a second address for your machine that is not `localhost`, for example its LAN IP (`ipconfig getifaddr en0` on macOS) or its Tailscale IP.

1. Compile and start the internal Storybook on all interfaces:
   ```sh
   yarn nx compile core
   cd code && yarn storybook:ui --host 0.0.0.0
   ```
2. In a new tab, open `http://<your-ip>:6006/?path=/story/core-component-test-basics--type`. Open it directly; do not go to it from another story.
   - Expected: the Interactions panel shows the play function as passed, and the input contains the typed text.
   - On `next`: the play function fails with `userEvent.type is not a function`.
3. Do the same for `http://<your-ip>:6006/?path=/story/core-user-event-view--events-have-their-view`. Expected: it passes. On `next` it fails with `userEvent.click is not a function`.
4. Open both stories at `http://localhost:6006/...`. Expected: they pass, as on `next`.
5. Over `<your-ip>`, run the browser console in the preview iframe: `'clipboard' in navigator`. Expected: `false`, the browser's own value. The context `userEvent` does not add a clipboard.

Areas to look at more closely: stories that use focus libraries (react-aria, Zag) over a non-localhost address, because the focus patch now also runs there.

prs.title: Core: Replace the story index's version counters with replaceable file slots
prs.manualTesting:
1. Start a sandbox dev server with `yarn task dev --template react-vite/default-ts --start-from auto` and open the URL it prints. The sandbox is in `../storybook-sandboxes/react-vite-default-ts`.
2. In the sandbox, create `src/stories/Probe.stories.ts` with `export default { title: 'Probe' }; export const Default = {};`.
3. Create `src/stories/Probe.mdx` with these lines:

4. Wait for `Probe` and its docs page in the sidebar.
5. Replace the content of `Probe.stories.ts` with `export default {` and save. The sidebar shows the indexing error.
6. Restore the content from step 2 and save. Do not touch the MDX file. The error goes away, and `<url>/index.json` answers 200 and lists `probe--docs` again.
7. Run `mkdir -p src/stories/tmp/deep`. Add a story file with its own title to `src/stories/tmp` and one to `src/stories/tmp/deep`. Wait for both in the sidebar.
8. Run `rm -rf src/stories/tmp`. Both stories leave the sidebar, `<url>/index.json` no longer lists them, and the selected story still renders.
9. Create and delete a story file a few times in a row, as in #37327. `<url>/index.json` answers 200 without that story every time.

prs.manualTesting:
1. Start a sandbox dev server with `yarn task dev --template react-vite/default-ts --start-from auto` and open the URL it prints. The sandbox is in `../storybook-sandboxes/react-vite-default-ts`. Run the next steps in the sandbox.
2. Run `mkdir -p src/stories/tmp/deep`. Create `src/stories/tmp/One.stories.ts` with `export default { title: 'Tmp/One' }; export const Default = {};` and `src/stories/tmp/deep/Two.stories.ts` with the title `Tmp/Two`. Wait for both in the sidebar.

4. Run `mv src/stories/tmp2 ./tmp2`. Both stories leave the sidebar, and `<url>/index.json` no longer lists them.

6. Open `src/stories/Button.stories.ts` in your editor and save it a few times. The Button stories never leave the sidebar.
7. Stop the server. Add `'./*.mdx'` to `stories` in `.storybook/main.ts` and start the server again. Create `.storybook/Intro.mdx` with `# Intro`. The docs page appears in the sidebar without a restart. Edit the heading, and the page follows. Delete the file and remove the entry from `main.ts`.

prs.title: Manager: Cut re-renders and store writes on story change
prs.manualTesting:
1. Build core and start the internal Storybook:
   ```bash
   yarn task compile -s compile && cd code && yarn storybook:ui
   ```
2. Open `core/argtype/String`, then click `Boolean` in the sidebar so the manager commits several times.
3. Press <kbd>alt</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd>, <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>alt</kbd>+<kbd>V</kbd>, <kbd>alt</kbd>+<kbd>=</kbd>, then <kbd>alt</kbd>+<kbd>0</kbd>: outline and measure toggle on, the viewport switches to the first preset, the zoom indicator goes to 110% and back to 100%.
4. Press <kbd>L</kbd> twice, then <kbd>K</kbd>: the locale toolbar must advance twice (en → es → zh) and step back once. The shortcut actions read the current global when they fire, so a stale value would get stuck after the first press.
5. In Settings → Keyboard shortcuts, change the locale "next" shortcut and the outline shortcut, then switch stories and toggle outline: both custom bindings must survive, and the old keys must do nothing. Before this PR a re-registration reset the binding to its default.
6. Click the `Click Me!` button in the preview: the Actions tab badge counts the event, and the badge disappears when switching story.
7. Record a story click in the browser performance panel: long tasks stay around 50–100 ms where they were about 400 ms before, and React DevTools' "highlight updates" no longer flashes the whole sidebar on every commit.

Areas most likely to regress: addon shortcuts (settings page listing, custom bindings, restoring defaults, menu items of third-party addons that set `showInMenu`) and any addon whose panel relied on receiving a new state object identity on every write.

prs.title: Core: Make the watch-story-specifiers test expectations separator-agnostic
prs.manualTesting:
No manual test is necessary: this PR changes test expectations only, not runtime behavior. Because path separators are identical on Linux, the focused suite was verified locally and the Windows behavior is proven by the path library semantics:

- `yarn vitest` (core project) on `code/core/src/core-server/utils/watch-story-specifiers.test.ts`: 15 passed, no type errors.
- `node -e "…resolve('C:\\Users\\ci\\repo\\__mockdata__','src')…"` with `pathe` → `C:/Users/ci/repo/__mockdata__/src` (forward slashes), while `node:path`'s `join` on the same inputs → `C:\Users\ci\repo\__mockdata__/src` (backslashes) — exactly the expected/received pair from the failing job. With this PR both sides of the assertion are `pathe`-normalized on Windows.
- `oxlint --report-unused-disable-directives-severity=error` on the touched file: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt --check`: clean.
